Params: After weeks of relentless elimination, only two teams remain. Team 09 has clawed its way into the final, and their run has been so brilliant that the crowd no longer remembers the team was patched together at the last minute.
The choice Adelyde made still sits heavy in her chest, but she has no room to grieve it. The constant motion is almost a mercy.
No one knows how this team grew into what it is today, one brutal match at a time.
At first, the only words between Adelyde and Arakna were clipped orders on the tactical channel, nothing more.
But the storm of fire forced them back-to-back whether they wanted it or not.
Shoulder to shoulder, boost after boost, each perfectly timed step, each cover given without a word, all of it says what neither of them can.
The night before the final, Adelyde leaves the training grounds and finds the team lounge's light still on.
Arakna is bent over the long table, working a needle through a large sheet of fabric under the glow of a single lamp.
How long are you gonna stand there? Come hold this corner for me.
She keeps sewing as she talks, hardly looking up. Only when Adelyde steps closer and holds down a corner of the fabric does she see what is taking shape.
Six chibi figures, all round and chubby, gathered on the cloth: Arakna, Adelyde, and Aristo, their own Team 09, and facing them, Helentine, Ophelia, and Greta, the opponents waiting in the final.
All six sit clustered together, plump and cheerful.
It's going up in the stands tomorrow. So, what do you think of my handiwork?
Helentine's team is on here too... and we're fighting them tomorrow.
Adelyde pokes at the Helentine chibi, lost in thought. The silly, round face pulls a small smile from her, even with the weight she has been carrying these past days.
The cloth just wasn't big enough.
Arakna slips the needle into her hair and lifts the fabric toward the lamp.
Otherwise I'd have stitched all 32 teams on here, and every single student at F.O.S.
Adelyde has every reason to believe she would do it. Arakna is already running her fingers along the edges of the fabric, measuring whether there is room for a few more figures.
F.O.S. gave me peace I hadn't felt in a long time. It's starting to feel like home.
So I'm supposed to look at this while fighting in the final? It's too cu—too unrealistic. Feels like it will sap everyone's fighting spirit.
Adelyde just barely keeps the word "cute" from escaping her mouth.
It's fine. Take a look at yourself first.

Her fingertip lands on a white-haired chibi. Her brow is drawn tight, her expression ready to snap to attention at any moment... And yet, on that round little body, the fierce look comes across as more endearing than intimidating.
Adelyde pokes at the little figure's brows, trying to press them flat.
That's totally you. In every photo since the day we met, you look like you're standing at attention for inspection.
Hey, do you remember that Huhu that snuck into the Kelpie on the Day of Enlightenment?
Adelyde's hand stops. "Do you remember..." No one has said those words to her in a very long time.
Ever since she came back from that dock, memory has been a dangerous thing. Behind the door of the present, there are pasts she cannot speak of.
And now, Arakna is the one who pushes that door open for her. A childhood hideout, full of treasures buried inside.
Adelyde opens her mouth, only to find her throat dry and her voice unsteady.
Yeah. It was so scared it stuck to me the entire time. Wouldn't stop shaking.
And? Who finally got it to settle down?
...Helentine. She crouched down, gave it a pat on the head, and the Huhu stopped shaking, just like that.
Right?! That's just her. The two of us tried everything and got nothing. She just looked at it, and it calmed right down.
They trade old stories, bits and pieces of childhood embarrassments, and little by little, smiles spread across the faces of two close friends who each carry their own worries.
Arakna notices it first. Her hands keep working as she speaks, her voice quiet.
Ade, you were never good at smiling. And after you started at F.O.S., you got even more serious.
I've said this before. When you keep that face straight, you look like one of those statues at the entrance to the Helio sector. When you smile, that's when you actually look like you.
Smile more, okay? I'll set the example.
Her eyes soften into crescents, and something of the old Arakna surfaces, the girl who was once as clear and untroubled as spring water, before the shell grew around her.

Adelyde lets her finger wander over the cloth, following the lines of her own journey, the lone passages and the ones walked beside another... There were moments she had wanted to smile but couldn't. Their number is beyond her. Beyond her courage, too.
Arakna, a lot might still happen from here. If...
The last stitch is sewn. Arakna bites off the thread and lifts the fabric high, where the six little figures hang in a row beneath the lamp.
No "ifs." Even if the sky comes down—
Oh right, come find me after the finals. I'll teach you how to make a decent drift bottle. That one you gave me was so ugly I couldn't sleep.
But you still keep it by your bed.
Go to sleep! No all-nighters for tomorrow's winners!
Outside, a sky full of stars spreads across the dark like a woven veil.

On the day of the final, Arakna's handiwork is hung by her colleagues from the paper in the most prominent spot in the stands. Six chibis who are meant to be fighting each other crowd together on a single support banner, making for an unusual sight.

Ladies and gentlemen, the match for today's final is maritime rescue. A ship damaged in a simulated storm, survivors trapped in compartments throughout, water levels rising without pause. Scoring is based on rescues, and knockdowns don't count.
If teams cooperate on a rescue, both earn points.
At both ends of the entrance tunnel, a flood of holographic light swallows the two teams.
Heavy waves strike the tilted deck, and the ship's frame groans as it starts to come apart. Adelyde and Arakna emerge from the passage almost simultaneously.
Adelyde slows at once and leans right. A moment later, the wall on her left collapses.
No more words are needed. Adelyde is already running in the direction Arakna pointed.
Water rises from below. Arakna is about to look for another route when Adelyde kicks open a side door, revealing a steep maintenance chute inside.
They slide into the darkness one after the other. Adelyde grabs Arakna's collar from behind, and Arakna uses the momentum to plant her feet. Together, they steady their landing.
They keep moving without a word.
It is just like the Atlantic Eye vessel simulation, only quieter, the idle chatter stripped away, leaving only perfect coordination.
Both teams race the clock, and before long, the match enters its second half.
One more survivor, third deck from the bottom! Blue team's already there!
Sis! Uh, I mean, Helentine, safety line's ready! The second you're out, we'll pull you up!
Ade, the path down is clear. I've got one on my shoulder, headed for the deck. You guys are up.
Two figures land at the same moment before the last remaining escape route. A structural warning blares overhead. The passage is dangerously unstable, and water has already reached their ankles.
They push ahead one after the other, forced to turn sideways to fit through the listing gap, chunks of the ceiling falling around them.
Even under these conditions, the two of them move at a pace that refuses to break.
Three years, and you're finally giving me a real fight.
Right back at you. Getting this close to someone from another family, aren't you worried your father will give you an earful?
Ever since you and Arakna finally fought together, you've been joking more. That face of yours isn't so stiff. I like it, Ade.
Family can wait. We're on the same track now, so—
Helentine suddenly picks up speed, pulling ahead. Adelyde is caught on a bent pipe and loses a beat.
Above, a panel of the hull has come loose, groaning as it drops, and Helentine is right under it.
She grabs Helentine's wrist and yanks her back. The bulkhead crashes down exactly where Helentine had been standing half a second earlier.
The recoil slams Adelyde into the pipes behind her, a dull ache spreading across her back. She stays bent, unable to rise.
In that breath, Helentine is almost at the corridor exit.
But she looks back at Adelyde.
She wades back, takes Adelyde's hand, and pulls her forward.
Side by side, they burst through the corridor exit.
After two hours of incredible competition, the match is officially over! Final score: 3280 to 3260! And the winner is—
The spreading water dissolves, the holographic scene stripping away layer by layer. A wall of noise crashes down from the dome.
Helentine sits on the floor, staring at her empty hands.
Then another hand enters her view.
She hesitates for a moment, then reaches out and takes it. After all the long shadows that had stood between them, nothing remains in the way.
Arakna crashes in from the side and throws her arms around both of them before they can steady themselves. The three of them stumble, laughing, and tumble into one another.
The golden trophy glints against the smiles of Team 09, and even Adelyde cannot hide her excitement. The winners' names have just been carved into its base, shining under the spotlight.
Arakna's hands tremble around the cup, so her two teammates steady her arms from either side, and together they lift it high amid the roar of the crowd.

Beside them, Helentine, who just lost the final, is the first to applaud. Ophelia, who had been huddled with Greta reviewing the match moments ago, still wears a look of reluctance, but she joins in at once.
The salute guns boom, and confetti of color fills the air, a glittering storm that lights up the faces of everyone present.
Family rifts, sorrows long buried, all of it fades beneath the golden fall. The girls, once scattered by distance, find their way back to each other.
Arakna... these past few years must've been hard on you. You look like you've lost weight.
A sudden pinch catches the black-haired girl in the soft spot at her waist.
That's muscle! Let's see if you've been slacking on your training—
Her long-prepared words of care are scattered by the sudden, ridiculous attack. Even Helentine, always steady, finds herself thrown off balance.
Okay, Arakna, leave her alone. She probably picked that line up from her father.
I know, I know. She's just like you, always so prim and proper around me. I just wanted to cheer her up!
The warm sea breeze at Port A054 seems to find them again. Helentine watches Adelyde and Arakna laughing, and a smile comes over her own face.
Helentine, will your father have an issue with you and Ophelia standing with us...?
His message is probably on its way already. Today was our match, after all.
Don't worry. He actually listens to the two of us more than you'd think.
More like he only listens to you, Sis. But we didn't win today...
That shot you made in the match, the one hitting the jammed hatch button, was seriously impressive.
The platinum-haired girl's self-mocking words are suddenly picked up and answered. She looks at her sister's friend in surprise and finds only sincerity and attention in Adelyde's eyes.
That kind of precision while floating in water... Not even three people in our year could pull it off. I'm one of them.
If you're interested, want to hit the range together sometime?
I-I don't need the winner's compliments to feel confident!
She lets her gaze float toward the falling confetti above, yet the curve at the corner of her mouth refuses to fade.
The line between the stands and the arena floor has vanished. Shouting cadets pour toward the center, carrying the banner stitched with those round little figures.
Come on, a moment like this deserves to be remembered!
She picks up markers from the cadets crowding around her and begins handing them out to everyone, from the competitors to the spectators who just came for the fun.
Then one is held out to Adelyde.
Don't you dare write some mood-killer like an apology.
She looks aside for just a second, brushing quickly at the edge of her eye. Then she faces Adelyde again, her gaze wet and pink, a smile still holding on her lips.
This marker means one thing: here, now, us.
Adelyde accepts the marker and leans over the cloth, signing her name in deliberate strokes beside the chibi with the tight expression and the white hair.
Arakna adds her own name beside her round little likeness.
There. Now, a new chapter's about to start, and this banner is our prologue.
Helentine, over here! We saved a spot for your team!
Helentine and Ophelia each leave their signatures, then sketch a plump little Huhu beside the names and write a brief note next to the little creature.
"Hope Sis wins next time"... Ophelia, this is a banner, not a wish tag.
Arakna shapes her left hand into a megaphone and lifts a corner of the banner with her right, turning toward the crowd gathering around them.
Hey, everyone! We used to have a tradition. Every year, we'd write our wishes down in a place. Not for the gods, but for the people right next to us!
This banner's for all of you now. Sign your name, write your wish, and whoever sees it helps make it real!
The crowd rushes in with a cheer. Names land on the fabric one after another, wishes crammed crookedly beside them, spreading until the banner is covered.
A middle-aged researcher steps up and adds her wish too.
"I hope my son grows up safe and healthy, and that his eyes always shine like stars."
Mom?! What are you doing down here?
What, a mom can't wish for her own son?
You can, you can, obviously you can!
The middle-aged engineer ruffles the boy's messy hair the way one might pet a small animal.
You've grown up so fast these years, my brave little star.
Obviously... ahem, Mom, stop it! This is so embarrassing...
Nearby, a crowd of rowdy students pushes Wells up to the banner. He adjusts his glasses and writes without hesitation:
<phonetic=Fiat  justitia   ruat   caelum.>"Let justice be done though the heavens fall."</phonetic>
<phonetic=Fiat justitia ruat caelum.>"Let justice be done though the heavens fall."</phonetic>
Tucked into the banner's least noticeable spot, a plain-faced student adds her name in letters barely visible to the eye. No one notices when she arrives. No one notices when she leaves.
Everyone, look to the dome! The closing ceremony begins!
The dome splits above them, and a fleet of small ceremonial drones streaks up in ribbons of gold. At the apex of their flight, they bloom at once, a tiny storm of silver and fire.
The crowd's cheer swells as three girls line up shoulder to shoulder before the banner, their faces raised to the glow.
...Back on Gardener Island, I made a wish. That when your wishes came true, we'd still be together watching the fireworks.
Your starship hasn't launched yet. Helentine's family stuff still isn't sorted... None of your wishes have come true yet.
But one day, they all will.
Arakna makes a silly face at Adelyde, the exact expression she used to wear as a child whenever she was up to something.
It is ridiculous, overdone, and it sends a flood of long-buried, careless days surging back into Adelyde's chest.
Light cascades over the raised faces below, and over the banner crowded with signatures and wishes.
No one sees the golden current that runs in the distance, or the faint gray figure standing within it, no brighter than a spark, observing all of this from across an immeasurable distance of time.
The figure makes no sound, and none is needed. That gaze rests on the white-haired girl who has finally found her way back to her friends, and those eyes bend into a soft, satisfied smile.
The golden current stirs again, carrying this silent traveler toward the next passage.
Many years later, long enough for Adelyde to have become an Instructor of F.O.S.,

she will hang this banner in the memorial hall, the banner that holds the brightest memories of the academy's finest, so that their glory, their conviction, and their spirit remain forever part of F.O.S.
So that no meeting and no parting, in any time or space, is ever erased.
